This was the first Open Race since Christmas, and although arranged in a hurry, proved quite a success. Syd. Roberts led the "Bels." home, closely followed by Bill Snell, Jack Bidgood and Bob Readman.

Jack Rutland, Fred Brunning, Syd Roberts, Alf. Harley and others, have always been ready with help and advice, and have repeatedly made offers of cash interest.
Talking of the B.N.L., the names of Charlie Redgrave, Syd Roberts, Jack Rutland and Fred Brunning should be mentioned for the practical help they have given to its Editor and Producer—Percy Wright.

Perhaps the biggest surprise of the season was Syd Roberts' win in the Met. 15 at Regents Park on 17th April. After a very steady start over the first five miles, he went through the field, eventually taking the lead about a mile and a half from home to win quite comfortably by nearly a minute.
Syd Roberts, maintaining his recent return to form, walked a good race to finish second to Norman Burt (S.W.C.). Once again, our fourth in succession, we won the Scratch Team Race.
Bob improved on his last year's time in once again winning the Police Ten Miles Championship, only 21secs. outside the record for the event; Syd Roberts was third.
Oscar, unfortunately, was unable to be present. He and Syd Roberts very sportingly supplied awards for the first two to finish.
Syd Roberts hasn't been very active this season as he had a bad bout of influenza. He has, however, captained the walkers again to good effect.
Joe Coleman, proposed by Syd. Roberts and Cyril Pateman, and Tommy Morrell, proposed by Harry Shields and Arthur Penny, were duly elected to this great honour.

Most of our lads walked extremely well and were ably assisted by Harry Churcher, Syd Roberts and Percy Wilson, but despite all their efforts, they were unable to do better than second place, with Charlie Churcher taking third individual honour.
